title: Hall effect in viscous flows of two-dimensional electrons in samples with edges of arbitrary roughness
authors: A. V. Gert, P. S. Alekseev
abstract: In ultra-clean conductors, fast inter-particle collisions can lead to the formation of a viscous electron fluid and realization of the hydrodynamic transport regime. Here we develop a theory of hydrodynamic magnetotransport of two-dimensional (2D) electrons in samples with low densities of defects and edges of arbitrary roughness. Within our model the roughness is described by a single parameter with the dimension of speed in the boundary conditions on sample edges. The electron-fluid flow profiles in long samples, as well as the corresponding longitudinal and Hall resistances, are calculated. The contribution to the Hall resistance associated with the relaxation processes exhibits a saturation in the limit of high magnetic field and a minimum as a function of the magnetic field for sufficiently rough edges. The minimum disappears as the edge roughness decreases or the sample width and bulk scattering by defects increase. These properties of the Hall resistance can serve as the signs to identify the hydrodynamic regime of electron transport in experiments and can be used to determine its parameters, in particular, the degree of edge roughness.
summary: This theoretical work models the magnetotransport of 2D electron fluids in samples with rough edges by treating the system hydrodynamically. It derives expressions for the Hall resistance correction, $\deltaho_{xy}(B)$, which is predicted to show a characteristic minimum at high magnetic fields when edge roughness is significant. This minimum provides a measurable signature to experimentally determine the degree of edge roughness.
main_problem: The paper develops a theory to describe the hydrodynamic magnetotransport of two-dimensional (2D) electron fluids in samples whose edges possess arbitrary roughness.
main_result: The Hall resistance correction, $\deltaho_{xy}(B)$, exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on the magnetic field, showing a minimum at sufficiently rough edges, which can be used as a diagnostic tool to measure edge roughness.
method: The analysis uses the Navier-Stokes equations for the electron fluid flow, incorporating boundary conditions derived from a local collision operator to model edge scattering.
model_or_system: The system is a 2D electron gas confined in a sample geometry, modeled as a viscous electron fluid. The theory accounts for bulk scattering (defects) and boundary scattering (edges) using a hydrodynamic approximation for the distribution function.
key_observables: Longitudinal and Hall resistances ($ho_{xx}, ho_{xy}$), and specifically the relaxation contribution to the Hall resistance, $\deltaho_{xy}(B)$.
important_parameters: Edge roughness parameter ($a$), sample width ($W$), bulk defect scattering rate ($\gamma_{imp}$), and the magnetic field ($B$).
main_assumptions: The theory relies on the hydrodynamic approximation for the distribution function and assumes the electron-electron collision time is much shorter than the impurity scattering time ($	au_{ee} \ll 	au_{imp}$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate velocity profiles, longitudinal resistivity, and the Hall correction ($\deltaho_{xy}$) for varying sample widths and edge roughness parameters, showing the minimum dependence on the magnetic field.
paper_structure: The paper builds the theory by defining the governing equations (Navier-Stokes, collision integrals) for the hydrodynamic flow. It then calculates the resistivities ($ho_{xx}, ho_{xy}$) and analyzes the magnetic field dependence of the Hall correction ($\deltaho_{xy}$), establishing diagnostic criteria based on the minimum value.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the use of hydrodynamic equations and the development of diagnostic signatures (like the minimum in $\deltaho_{xy}$) to characterize boundary conditions is relevant to understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in mesoscopic systems.
